clean-5.describes: five well-formed events and NO checkpoint — internally consistent, cryptographically unanchored

clean-3.describes: three well-formed events and no checkpoint; the subject of the manifest.sig validity cases

nested-root.describes: five events, preceded by an entry one directory below the archive root

tampered-event.describes: five events with seq 3's content edited and its stored event_hash left alone, then re-signed over the tampered file so the content-hash check PASSES — the chain check is what must catch it

seq-gap.describes: five events with seq 3 removed, so seq 4 follows seq 2

shadowed-events.describes: five signed events, plus an UNSIGNED two-event `x/events.json` placed earlier in the archive. The manifest covers only the root copy. A verdict that found its chain by basename would describe the shadow — two events — while integrity reported the five it never read

anchored-e2e.describes: the committed `anchored/` fixture — its checkpoints and anchors.json — packed into a signed bundle, so the end-to-end path can pull anchors.json back out of a real archive. Its events.json is empty: this case is about anchoring, and the chain verdict is asserted by the cases above

checkpointed-4.describes: four events anchored by a checkpoint signed at 2026-06-14T01:00:00.000Z; the validity-window cases put their trust-key window around that instant
